- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to account for downward surprise.
- Model frequently overshoots after sharp price spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days); apply a 2–5 day decay filter to smooth out overreaction.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 60–65), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with recent 5-day moving average.
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period momentum; add 1–2% upward bias if sentiment turns bullish in last 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “high-low” swings (e.g., 0.67 → 0.00 → 0.67), model misreads trend; use sentiment-weighted average of last 7 days to anchor forecast.
